references.text: Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, is mentioned again as chosen by God to teach others in craftsmanship.
Oholiab is mentioned together with Bezalel as those who received wisdom and understanding from God to carry out the work on the sanctuary.
Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, is described as an engraver, artist, and weaver in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.
God gives wisdom to all who have a willing heart, so that they can make Aaron's priestly garments.
The context where Bezalel is first appointed and filled with God's Spirit, wisdom, and understanding for every kind of craft.
All those among the Israelites who have a willing heart are encouraged to come and make everything the Lord has commanded.
Solomon asks God for a willing heart, which shows the same principle that God gives wisdom to people.
Proverbs confirms that the Lord gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
James teaches that whoever lacks wisdom should ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach.
Direct narrative connection: The fulfillment of the same gift of wisdom given in chapter 31.
Direct narrative connection: Confirmation that the work was carried out through the wisdom given.
